messages:
Taylor Morgan: hey all, first-day question. Kandji shows my device as enrolled but Homebrew won't install: "brew: permission denied" and attempts to run a native binary prompt "developer tool needs Rosetta". i'm on macOS Sonoma 14.2 on an M2. i don't have admin rights yet, and the OS keeps blocking a system extension prompt in Security & Privacy. any safe way to get my dev tools installed?
Ravi Kapoor: welcome @Taylor! we try to avoid granting permanent admin. two common flows: 1) short-lived local admin via Kandji (24h) or 2) remote allow-listing of the specific kernel ext / notarized binary via the MDM. which would you prefer?
Taylor Morgan: prefer not to run as admin if we can avoid it. what does remote allow-listing look like?
IT Helpdesk Bot: Auto-check: device serial C02M2EXAMPLE enrolled. Kandji jobs available: "bootstrap-local-admin" (24h), "allow-notarized-binary" (requires hash and notarization cert), "allow-kext" (requires team ID). Open ticket #HWI-4899 created for request.
Marta Ruiz: hi @Taylor — quick troubleshooting: can you paste the exact brew install error and run 

```
spctl --status
sudo xattr -lr /usr/local/bin | head -n 20
```

so we can see Gatekeeper status and quarantine flags. If the installer is asking for Rosetta, we can install Rosetta via MDM command so arm64 translation is available without local admin interaction.
Taylor Morgan: spctl output: "assessments enabled". brew error: "/opt/homebrew/bin/brew: Permission denied" when running install script. xattr shows quarantined on a few downloaded things.
Ravi Kapoor: sounds like quarantine and gatekeeper are blocking unsigned helper scripts. two safe options: - we can push a Kandji job to install Rosetta and run a signed bootstrap script (allow-notarized-binary) OR - we can briefly give you "onboard-temp" admin and you run installs, then we revoke. which works on your schedule?
Taylor Morgan: i'm in meetings most of the day, so short-lived admin would be easiest. i'll schedule a 30-min window now.
Marta Ruiz: approved. creating temp admin now. Kandji job queued.
IT Helpdesk Bot: Kandji: job "bootstrap-local-admin" targeted at C02M2EXAMPLE queued by Marta Ruiz. Account created: onboard-temp. Expiration: 24h. Ticket updated #HWI-4899.
Ravi Kapoor: when you log in as onboard-temp, run the Rosetta installer (no GUI prompt): 

```
sudo /usr/sbin/softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
```

That will install required translation and Homebrew. After installs, run `sudo dseditgroup -o delete -q groupname`? (no, ignore that) — sorry. just let us know when done and we'll revoke the temp admin.
Taylor Morgan: logged in as onboard-temp, Rosetta installed fine. Homebrew install succeeded. i'm seeing one remaining system prompt in System Settings > Privacy & Security asking to allow a kernel extension from "com.example.driver" but the allow button is greyed out (says admin approval required).
Marta Ruiz: that greyed allow happens if the kext is already blocked at a lower level or the vendor ID isn't a match. can you paste the output of: 

```
kmutil showloaded | grep example || true
sudo kextstat | grep -i example || true
```

If it's blocked, we can either 1) ask the vendor to notarize and we allow via MDM OR 2) we can escalate to security for a time-limited exception. Which is this driver for?
Taylor Morgan: it's the USB serial driver for the dev board we use in the hardware team. vendor is third-party.
Ravi Kapoor: for hardware dev stuff, security will usually grant an exception if it's just for onboarding. I'll open a security exception with the vendor's team ID and file hash. Marta, can you keep the temp admin active until we complete the exception?
Marta Ruiz: done. Security ticket SE-1223 created; requested vendor artifacts. Temp admin will remain until we confirm. Taylor, once you finish setup please ping here and we'll revoke.
Taylor Morgan: finished installs, verified board enumerates over USB, all good. thanks for the quick help! :tada: i've added a note to my onboarding checklist to request temp admin during first-dev setup.
Ravi Kapoor: great. revoking temp account now.
IT Helpdesk Bot: Kandji: job "revoke-local-admin" executed for C02M2EXAMPLE. onboard-temp removed. Ticket #HWI-4899 updated: resolved.
Marta Ruiz: thanks @Taylor. if security approves the vendor exception later we'll update the runbook so future new hires don't need the temp admin step. please drop a short blurb in #docs-onboarding.
Taylor Morgan: will do. appreciate the help!
